blogs.title: The CA-125 Trap: Interpreting Biomarkers in Pregnancy
blogs.description: A deep dive into the pitfalls of using CA-125 for the diagnosis of ovarian malignancies during pregnancy. This post discusses the physiological fluctuations of the marker across trimesters and why isolated elevations—like those seen in this case—should be interpreted with caution to avoid unnecessary oncological anxiety or over-intervention.

blogs.title: Dyspnea in the Second Trimester: When it's Not a Pulmonary Embolism
blogs.description: Analyzing the presentation of restrictive lung disease caused by massive abdominal masses. This post focuses on the differential diagnosis of dyspnea in the pregnant patient, emphasizing the 'steric bulk' effect where extreme abdominal pressure mimics cardiac or pulmonary failure, and the role of semi-orthostatic positioning in symptomatic relief.

blogs.title: To Cut or Not to Cut: The Timing of Myomectomy During Pregnancy
blogs.description: An exploration of the clinical tensions between the conservative 'wait until postpartum' approach and the need for urgent surgical intervention. This post analyzes the specific indicators that triggered surgery in this case—torsion, leaking, and respiratory compromise—and discusses the risks of preterm labor versus the risks of myoma necrosis.

blogs.title: Seeing Through the Gravid Uterus: US vs. MRI for Pelvic Masses
blogs.description: A practical comparison of imaging modalities when evaluating atypical abdominal masses in pregnancy. This post discusses the limitations of ultrasound in identifying pedunculated stalks in the presence of a large uterus and the utility of non-contrast MRI in determining the distance between a mass and the uterine cavity to guide surgical planning.

blogs.title: Blocking the Exit: How Myoma Location Dictates Delivery Mode
blogs.description: A discussion on the anatomical considerations of uterine leiomyomas and their impact on the expulsive phase of labor. Using the caudal mass from this case as a primary example, this post explains why location—rather than just size—is the deciding factor in choosing an elective caesarean section to avoid obstructed labor.
